 Move beyond pledges to end recurring haze crisis, Lee Lam Thye tells Asean leaders 
 KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has proposed expanding the funding sources of the existing Asean Haze Fund to ensure more sustainable financing for efforts to prevent and tackle transboundary haze, rather than establishing a new fund.
 The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry said in a parliamentary written reply that the proposal, known as the Sustainable Haze Fund, would broaden contributions beyond Asean member states to include international organisations, regional financial institutions, donor agencies and other stakeholders.
 The ministry was responding to Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian), who asked if the government would propose a special Asean fund with mandatory contributions from member states to finance fire prevention, firefighting operations, ecosystem restoration and assistance for haze victims.
 The ministry said Malaysia had presented the proposal at the 27th Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee Meeting on Trans-boundary Haze Pollution in Bali, Indonesia, in July.
 Malaysia had also proposed exploring potential contributions from the agriculture and insurance sectors, as well as health-related entities, based on the principle of shared responsibility. 
 The existing fund was established under Article 20 of the Asean Agreement on Trans-boundary Haze Pollution, with an initial contribution of US$500,000 from Asean member states.
